name: Alhambra
_about: THE ALHAMBRA as Muhammad V left it (c. 1370-1391), before any Christian work: the red walls round the Sabika hill with their towers and gates (the Justicia, the Vino, the Armas, the Siete Suelos); the Alcazaba and its soldiers' quarter; the Nasrid palaces -- the Mexuar and the Cuarto Dorado, Comares with the Court of the Myrtles and the Hall of the Ambassadors in its tower, the royal baths, the Palace of the Lions with its 124 columns, its pavilions, the Two Sisters and the Abencerrajes under their muqarnas domes, the Lindaraja garden open to the valley; the Partal and its pond; the medina with its great mosque where Santa Maria stands, the baths, the palaces of the Calle Real and its houses; across the ravine the GENERALIFE -- the Court of the Water Channel between its pavilions, the west gallery, the Sala Regia and Ismail I's tower, the Sultana's garden, the water stair, the orchards -- with the Albercon and the Silla del Moro above. Built by tools/archgen/alhambra.py from the components of tools/archgen/andalusi.py (its docstring: what is sourced, what is estimated, what is left out). x east, z south.

mexuar._about: the MEXUAR, the council hall (Ismail I, 1317; remade by Muhammad V), its lantern on four columns inside, and the rooms down to the Machuca court

mexuar oratory._about: its oratory, out over the wall toward the Albaicin, the windows north

machuca paving._about: the Machuca court, before the Mexuar

cuarto dorado portico._about: the Cuarto Dorado's portico of three arches

cuarto dorado._about: the Cuarto Dorado, its ceiling gilded under the Catholic Monarchs -- here as Muhammad V left it

comares facade._about: the COMARES FACADE (1370): Muhammad V's throne front, two doors under a band of windows, the court of the Cuarto Dorado before it

comares facade eave._about: its great carved eave of cedar

myrtles paving._about: the COURT OF THE MYRTLES (Comares, Yusuf I and Muhammad V): white marble round the pool

myrtles pool water._about: the pool, 34 m long, brim-full: the porticoes and the tower stand in it

myrtle hedges._about: the clipped myrtles along the pool's sides

myrtles north portico._about: the north portico: seven arches before the Sala de la Barca

myrtles south portico._about: the south portico, with the gallery over it

sala de la barca._about: the SALA DE LA BARCA, the antechamber, its wooden vault an upturned hull

myrtles west range._about: the ranges along the court: the women's rooms, two storeys, doors and windows on the court

myrtles south range._about: the south range (pulled down for Charles V's palace; rebuilt)

royal baths._about: the ROYAL BATHS of Comares (Ismail I): the Sala de las Camas, then the vaulted warm and hot rooms, half sunk in the hill

bath vaults._about: the baths' vaults over the roof, pierced with star-shaped skylights (the finish's)

lions paving._about: the COURT OF THE LIONS: 28.5 x 15.7 m, marble

lions north portico._about: its galleries: 124 columns, the arches stilted, the walls over them lace of plaster

lions west pavilion._about: the two pavilions standing out into the court at its ends, each a small qubba on clustered columns

lions fountain lions._about: the FOUNTAIN OF THE LIONS: twelve lions of marble, the water from their mouths

fountain basin._about: the twelve-sided basin on their backs, Ibn Zamrak's verses round its rim

channels._about: the channels from the fountain to the pavilions and the halls, the water flowing into the rooms

lions north range._about: the north range, the Two Sisters' hall rising in its middle

dos hermanas._about: the HALL OF THE TWO SISTERS: the muqarnas dome of some five thousand cells over its drum of windows

daraxa mirador._about: the MIRADOR OF DARAXA, the lady's window on the garden and the city below

abencerrajes._about: the HALL OF THE ABENCERRAJES: its star of muqarnas over the fountain

mocarabes._about: the Hall of the Mocarabes, the court's vestibule

sala de los reyes._about: the HALL OF THE KINGS: three domed alcoves behind triple arches, the painted leather vaults

cypress foliage._about: a dark flame, swelling from its foot ...

partal portico._about: THE PARTAL: a portico of five arches on the pond, the Damas tower behind it

partal oratory._about: the Partal's ORATORY (Yusuf I), its mihrab in a niche to the south-east, the windows out over the wall

partal house._about: the house beside it (Astasio de Bracamonte's)

acequia paving._about: THE GENERALIFE: the COURT OF THE WATER CHANNEL, 50 m long, the acequia down its middle between sunk beds

acequia channel water._about: the channel, the Acequia Real's water running through the court

acequia beds._about: the beds, sunk under the walks: myrtle, roses, orange trees

generalife north portico._about: the NORTH PAVILION: its portico of five arches on the court (the gallery over it is of 1494: left out)

sala regia._about: the SALA REGIA behind it, its triple arch, the windows over the city

generalife west gallery._about: the WEST GALLERY: eighteen arches on the court, windows in its back wall over the Alhambra

generalife mirador._about: its MIRADOR, standing out over the slope in the gallery's middle

generalife east range._about: the east range, rooms on two floors

sultana paving._about: the garden court beside it (the Sultana's: its galleries of 1584 left out)

generalife entrance paving._about: the ENTRANCE COURTS below the palace (the Polo and the Descabalgamiento)

generalife gate._about: its gate, before the wall's outer face

generalife entrance stair._about: the stair up to the court

mosque._about: THE GREAT MOSQUE of the Alhambra (Muhammad III, 1305): a hall of three naves, the qibla wall to the south

mosque arcade 1._about: its arcades, the naves' arches on marble columns

mosque roofs._about: a gable roof of tiles over each nave

mihrab._about: the octagonal mihrab, out from the qibla wall

mosque court paving._about: the court, orange trees in rows on the naves' axes

mosque minaret._about: the minaret at the court's corner

mosque baths._about: the MOSQUE'S BATHS (1305): the dressing hall, the cold, warm and hot rooms

yusuf III palace paving._about: the PALACE OF YUSUF III (1408-17's rebuilding of an older one): its court and pool, rebuilt from the excavated plan

yusuf III palace cypress foliage._about: a dark flame, swelling from its foot ...

abencerrajes palace paving._about: the palace of the Abencerrajes, blown up in 1812: rebuilt

abencerrajes palace cypress foliage._about: a dark flame, swelling from its foot ...

san francisco palace paving._about: the Nasrid palace under the convent of San Francisco (Yusuf I's), its court and pool

san francisco palace cypress foliage._about: a dark flame, swelling from its foot ...

city wall._about: THE WALL round the palace-city, some two kilometres of rammed earth and lime on the Sabika's edge, its walk 9 m over the ground

city wall breastwork 1._about: the breastwork along the walk's outer edge

city wall merlons._about: the square merlons, one every two metres

alcazaba wall._about: the ALCAZABA's own walls, the citadel at the hill's western point (9th-13th c.)

alcazaba wall breastwork 1._about: the breastwork along the walk's outer edge

alcazaba wall merlons._about: the square merlons, one every two metres

armas tower gate._about: its gate: a great horseshoe arch in its alfiz, the passage turning inside

vino gate gate 1._about: its gate: a great horseshoe arch in its alfiz, the passage turning inside

vino gate gate 2._about: its gate: a great horseshoe arch in its alfiz, the passage turning inside

justicia tower gate._about: its gate: a great horseshoe arch in its alfiz, the passage turning inside

siete suelos tower gate._about: its gate: a great horseshoe arch in its alfiz, the passage turning inside

ismail tower._about: the TOWER OF ISMAIL I behind the Sala Regia, its hall a mirador over the Darro

generalife cypress foliage._about: a dark flame, swelling from its foot ...

water stair 1._about: the WATER STAIR (Escalera del Agua): three flights and their landings up to the oratory

water stair parapet north._about: its parapets, the water running down a channel cut in their tops

generalife oratory._about: the small ORATORY at the stair's head (the Romantic mirador of 1836 stands near it now)

silla del moro._about: the SILLA DEL MORO (the castle of Santa Elena) on the hill over the Generalife, guarding the Acequia Real

silla del moro breastwork 1._about: the breastwork along the walk's outer edge

silla del moro merlons._about: the square merlons, one every two metres

albercon._about: the ALBERCON ARABE: the tank the Acequia Real filled, the orchards' water

huerta orange trunks._about: the ORCHARDS of the Generalife (the Huerta Grande, the Merceria): fruit trees on the terraces

houses 1._about: the medina's houses: whitewashed walls round a court, blind to the lane

palaces floor._about: the platforms the buildings stand on: walls of rubble up from the hill, filled, paved

hill._about: the Sabika hill as the IGN's 5 m terrain model has it, 745 m at y 0: cut level under the palaces and the medina's buildings, let down to the world's ground at the frame's edge
